data.body:
LANDED AND VERIFIED.

Change 1061 ('c083: tolerate untracked tracker files on signing') — LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, SUBMITTED and MERGED to main at 2026-07-30 21:50:08 UTC. On origin/main as commit 032f30fdc (Gerrit rebased on submit under Rebase-If-Necessary, so the landed sha differs from the locally authored b28c1b2e2).

ROOT CAUSE (proven, and a CORRECTION to this ticket's original filing): resign.py:146 called generation.collect(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root) omitting ignore_untracked, which defaults to False and reaches tracker_head_sha's strict 'git status --porcelain' (untracked INCLUDED) rather than '--untracked-files=no'. Any untracked path made the output non-empty -> store-read-failure. The originally-filed suspect (attest.py:406) was REFUTED as the source of this symptom: the message is emitted only at resign.py:153 wrapping generation.collect, and attest.py is not on that path (it is a sibling, fixed here too).

DISCRIMINATING EXPERIMENT (isolated temp git repo, runtime): strict RAISED store-read-failure for an untracked file regardless of NAME or CONTENT — which refutes the competing 'partial-JSON parse failure' hypothesis, since the check is purely git-status and content-agnostic. ignore_untracked=True succeeded and returned the SAME head sha as the clean-tree control, confirming untracked files genuinely cannot change the fingerprinted answer. TRACKED-dirty raised under BOTH settings, so the fix does not weaken the real guarantee.

SITES FIXED (4): resign.py (the confirmed defect), orchestrator.py's drift-refresh probe (previously swallowed by 'except Exception: return None', so a stray file SILENTLY forced a full multi-pass LLM re-review instead of the cheap probe — a money/latency defect with no error), and the two fallback collects in attest.py.

TESTS: three added to tests/unit/test_plan_relation_snapshot.py beside the two existing d7cb-22ae regression tests. Each was confirmed RED first for the right reason (reason string containing store-read-failure), with a CLEAN-tracker control asserting first so a red could not come from a broken fixture. The tests were HELD OUT of the implementing subagent's working tree entirely. Mutation check: re-introducing the exact root cause at resign.py returned both tolerance tests to RED; restoring the fix returned them to GREEN — the tests have teeth.

CONCURRENCY (operator requirement): this machine runs many sessions against ONE .tickets-tracker, symlinked into every session, so untracked paths there are the NORMAL transient state of another session's in-flight atomic write, not merely crash debris. The strict check therefore made signing RACE other sessions, with the failure rate scaling with concurrency. A test drives a live churning-writer thread to pin this. The fix deliberately does NOT clean up stray temp files — deleting one could destroy a concurrent writer's in-flight event. Tolerate, never tidy.

REPLICATION: with the exact original field condition reconstructed (two orphaned .tmp-event-* files of the same shape as the real ones), the function the CLI invokes now returns {ok: true, signed: true, reason: 're-signed the plan-review attestation from the latest REVIEW_RESULT sidecar (no LLM review re-run)'}. Pre-fix this returned store-read-failure.

GATES: make lint clean, make typecheck clean (398 files), full suite 8022 passed / 73 skipped / 0 failed. Defaults on tracker_head_sha / collect_plan_relation_snapshot / generation.collect were left STRICT so any future caller must opt in deliberately.

FOLLOW-UP FILED: c6c9-cba0-1aa4-47eb — attest.py was at 799/800 against the module-size hard cap, so this two-call-site change only fit by importing the function directly to avoid an E501 wrap, landing the file at EXACTLY 800 with zero headroom. It also forced the explanatory comments out of attest.py and down to a pointer, i.e. the cap is now shaping documentation quality.
